analysis: What changed versus the 8:00 AM brief: the tape flipped green by midday. The S&P went from -0.29% at 10:31 AM ET to +0.20% at 11:52 AM ET, with the Nasdaq and Dow also positive, and Apple hit an all-time high. The containment read is intact: five of six megacaps are green and NVDA, while still -4.8%, has held well above its $148.80 open low on enormous volume (495M shares vs a 154M average). The new pressure is the analyst pile-on rather than the resignation itself: at least seven firms cut NVDA targets or ratings today, Bernstein slashing to $200 from $400. The bigger headwind remains rates, not Nvidia: the 10-year rose for a fifth straight session to 5.09% (+9 bp on the day), which is what is pinning small caps (Russell -0.71%) and keeping gold and bitcoin down ~3%. The AI rotation story keeps widening: Broadcom +5% while Nebius is down 20%+ after guiding 2027 capex to a $43B midpoint vs ~$29B expected. Signal vs noise: the resignation, Kress as interim CEO, the claims and home-sales prints, and the analyst actions are confirmed signal. The Trump/Cook succession post is theater — no indication Cook wants the job — and the Srouji report is single-source. AI-generated blogs claiming Huang never resigned are contradicted by Nvidia's own announcement and the WSJ; treat them as noise. The tape stays fragile into Cisco and Applied Materials after the close, with Friday's PPI the next macro test.

community_signals.takeaway: Discussion of the resignation itself (100 comments), now focused on the second affair, the board's investigation, and who could credibly succeed Huang — the conversation has moved past the initial shock into succession mechanics and governance fallout.
community_signals.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after reports of second affair deepened scandal

headlines.headline: Nvidia kept recovering into midday: $165.38 (-4.8% vs Wednesday's $173.73 close) at ~11:56 AM ET, well off the $148.80 open low, on 495M shares vs a 154M average. But the analyst pile-on accelerated: Oppenheimer, KeyCorp, William Blair and Melius all downgraded today, Bernstein cut its target to $200 from $400 and Stifel to $205 from $315, Cantor to $250 from $350.
headlines.why_it_matters: Buyers keep defending above the panic low, but the wave of target cuts caps the bounce — the stock is now a leadership-discount story with a moving analyst anchor.

headlines.headline: The indexes flipped positive by midday: at 11:52 AM ET the S&P 500 was 7,634.68 (+0.20%), the Nasdaq 25,502.32 (+0.14%) and the Dow 52,649.25 (+0.31%). Small caps still lag: the Russell 2000 was -0.71%. Six of 11 sectors were green, energy leading at +1.67%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The morning dip got bought — the tape is stabilizing rather than deteriorating, with the selling still concentrated in AI names and small caps, not broad-based.

headlines.headline: Apple hit an all-time high Thursday, bucking the tech wreck: $357.31 (+0.5%) at ~11:56 AM ET, on track for a fourth straight week of gains and in a buy zone above a $344.57 pivot.
headlines.why_it_matters: Apple's strength while Nvidia is still down ~5% is the clearest containment signal — money is rotating within big tech, not leaving it.

headlines.headline: President Trump posted on Truth Social that Apple's Tim Cook should replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO: 'A Legend replaces a Legend!' Cook stepped down as Apple CEO on Sept. 1 and is now executive chairman. There is no indication Cook wants the job, and Nvidia's board is running its own search.
headlines.why_it_matters: Political theater around the succession, not a real candidate — it keeps the CEO-search story in the headlines but changes nothing about the board's process.

headlines.headline: Semafor reported Apple's hardware chief Johny Srouji is under consideration for the Nvidia CEO job, citing a person familiar with the matter. The report came before Thursday's resignation announcement.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source, unconfirmed — treat as fragile. If real, it would mean the board is looking outside the chip industry's usual names, but one report is not a shortlist.

headlines.headline: Trump posted on Truth Social on Iran: 'We don't need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed. We've got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we've got their Strait!' WTI ticked up to $86.98 (+0.52%) after the post.
headlines.why_it_matters: Rhetoric is keeping an oil-risk premium in the tape — energy was the day's best sector (+1.67%) on the back of it.

headlines.headline: Nebius (NBIS) sank more than 20% despite beating Q3 estimates (loss of $0.13/share vs $0.72 expected; revenue $981M, +511% YoY, vs $907M expected). The 2027 capex guide came in at a $43B midpoint vs ~$29B expected, and 2026 spending was raised to a $27B midpoint from $23B.
headlines.why_it_matters: The market is now punishing AI infrastructure spending plans, not rewarding growth — a capex-discipline read that matters for the whole neocloud/AI buildout trade.

headlines.headline: The other megacaps were mostly green at midday: Alphabet $300.07 (+2.3%), Amazon $269.78 (+1.4%), Microsoft $527.66 (+1.3%), Tesla $392.01 (+0.3%), while Meta $626.25 (-0.4%) was the only loser. Broadcom rose ~5% as the AI rotation extended.
headlines.why_it_matters: Five of six megacaps green with NVDA still down ~5% keeps the containment read — the market is treating this as a single-company governance shock, not a megacap re-rating.
